% AFTER path_resolve+strip_suffix builtins + WORKSPACE_PACKAGE nodes:
module_file(F) :- node(M, "MODULE"), attr(M, "file", F).
% rank-0: exact (specifier already has extension)
cand0(I, R) :- spec(I, F, S), path_resolve(F, S, R), module_file(R).
% rank-1: extension swap .js→.ts (one clause per (from,to) pair)
cand1(I, R) :- spec(I, F, S), path_resolve(F, S, P), strip_suffix(P, ".js", B), concat(B, ".ts", R), module_file(R).
% rank-2: append extension; rank-3: /index.<ext> — concat chains, one clause per ext
cand2(I, R) :- spec(I, F, S), path_resolve(F, S, P), concat(P, ".ts", R), module_file(R).
cand3(I, R) :- spec(I, F, S), path_resolve(F, S, P), concat(P, "/index.ts", R), module_file(R).
has0(I) :- cand0(I, _).  has01(I) :- cand0(I,_). has01(I) :- cand1(I,_).
resolved(I, R) :- cand0(I, R).
resolved(I, R) :- cand1(I, R), \+ has0(I).
resolved(I, R) :- cand2(I, R), \+ has01(I).  % ...ladder continues
% workspace exact-match arm:
resolved(I, R) :- spec(I, _, S), node(W, "WORKSPACE_PACKAGE"), attr(W, "name", S), attr(W, "file", R), module_file(R).

spec.expected_speedup_rationale: The 76s wall is dominated by IPC and duplicated indexing, not resolution math: build-index streams the ENTIRE node set to the Haskell daemon (200MB max_message_size pool config, main.rs:1114-1120), then every file round-trips through resolve-file (8 resolvers re-run per file, Main.hs:206-215), then a SECOND full-graph streaming pass runs just two more resolvers (main.rs:1152-1160), all over msgpack with per-checkpoint commits. The packs eliminate every byte of that IPC: they run in-engine directly over LSM segments. Proven baseline on this exact graph: a 4-rule pack with negation over the 415k-node dogfood graph = 4-20s scratch (method_calls/shape_verifier class). The wave-1 expressible packs (~6 packs: imports-module, builtins×2, same-file-calls, local-refs, cross-file-calls, this-method-calls) share the same dominant base scans (CALL/REFERENCE/IMPORT_BINDING + name/file attr probes, served by the build-once hash-join). Estimate 15-40s total scratch → ~2-5× wall improvement, NOT 10×: these packs use negation and (builtins) node materialization, so maintain-incremental refuses them and the scratch floor applies (acceptable per the stated constraint). The structural wins beyond wall-clock: the Haskell daemon process/binary disappears from the JS path, the logic becomes inspectable/why()-able, and each pack that later sheds its negation (or when maintain learns stratified negation) drops to O(delta) maintenance.

spec.differential_acceptance:
Setup: freeze ONE dogfood snapshot — full `analyze` on the grafema repo with the legacy resolver chain, copy .grafema/grafema.rfdb to A (resolver baseline) and to B-pre (same state MINUS the rust-resolve commits; obtain by re-running analyze with the rust resolve section disabled, or by filtering A's edges by the resolver's own provenance, below). Both engines run on identical EDB.

Keying: every comparison row is (src_semantic_id, edge_type, dst_semantic_id) — u128 ids are BLAKE3(semantic_id) (storage_glue.rs:46), so semantic-id-keyed dumps are stable across copies. Dump via the server (datalog query r(S,D) :- edge(S,D,"CALLS"). + node-id→semantic-id resolution through the existing dump/query path), sort, diff with comm -3.

Side identification — both sides are self-labeling: (a) resolver edges carry meta resolvedVia ∈ {rust-calls, rust-cross-method, rust-dyn-dispatch, runtime-globals} (RustCallResolution.hs:78, RustCrossMethodCalls.hs:207,222, RuntimeGlobals.hs:264) and IMPORTS_FROM/IMPLEMENTS are filtered by src node type (IMPORT/IMPORT_BINDING/STRUCT) + file ends_with('.rs'); (b) pack edges carry the engine provenance stamp (_source = rule hash + _generation) AND the same resolvedVia meta column by construction of the draft heads. Compare endpoint sets and the resolvedVia/receiverType meta VALUES; exclude _source/_generation keys.

Per-pack procedure and expectations:
1. rust_calls pack on B-pre → dump CALLS(resolvedVia=rust-calls) → diff vs A's same-filter set. EXPECTED: pack ⊇ resolver, exactly equal except the duplicate-(file,name) class. Every pack-only row must be auto-classified by a companion checker query: dup_fn(File,N) :- node(F1,"FUNCTION"),attr(F1,"file",File),attr(F1,"name",N),node(F2,"FUNCTION"),attr(F2,"file",File),attr(F2,"name",N),neq(F1,F2). — a pack-only edge whose target is in a dup_fn group is CLASSIFIED; anything else FAILS.
2. cross-methods (substrate + resolved-constructor pack, ordered after rust_calls): EXPECTED a two-sided diff, fully partitioned: resolver-only rows must each match one of the BLOCKED strategies — verified by re-running the resolver with strategy-tagging (its receiverType/resolvedVia meta + the stderr counters '[rust-cross-methods] … resolved=N', Hs:161-167, give per-strategy totals); the partition must sum to the diff count exactly. Pack-only rows must each witness a READS_FROM/ASSIGNED_FROM/CALLS/HAS_METHOD chain — checked with explain/why() or a diagnostic query re-deriving the row; these are the scope-resolved-receiver precision deltas. Target gate at this stage: pack∩resolver / resolver ≥ the constructor-strategy share, 0 unclassified rows on either side. FULL parity (18,679-edge equality modulo dup classes) is gated on node_attr landing; re-run the same diff then with EXPECTED: pack ⊇ resolver, pack-only rows all in dup-name or scope-precision classes.
3. rust-trait-resolve (post-node_attr): EXPECTED exact equality, except duplicate-name STRUCT/TRAIT superset rows classified by the analogous dup_struct/dup_trait checker.
4. rust-imports (post-string-builtins): EXPECTED exact equality on IMPORT→MODULE (the transform is deterministic and total); IMPORT_BINDING→decl equal modulo duplicate-export superset class. Cross-check counts against the resolver's stderr line 'rust-resolve: N module edges, M binding edges' (Hs:225-227).
5. rust-globals: stays out of scope until external-table ingestion; differential N/A.

Idempotence + ownership checks per pack: run the pack TWICE on B — second run must be a no-op (additive dedup); run pack on A (on top of resolver edges) — edge count must not change (proves additive parity); GLOBAL/ISSUE-style minted nodes N/A here.

Acceptance gate (per pack): |unclassified diff rows| = 0, where classification is mechanical (companion .dl checker queries, no manual triage), plus the count cross-check against the resolver's own stderr totals on the same frozen snapshot. Record the classified-delta counts in the pack header as the parity contract (the axum_routes.dl 'documented parity deltas' convention).
spec.expected_speedup_rationale: The 76s wall is dominated by transport and per-command rework, not by resolution logic: stream_and_resolve_single_worker (plugin.rs:1274-1349) (a) collects ALL resolve nodes by looping ~30 node types through query_nodes_by_type IPC round-trips, (b) JSON-converts each wire node incl. metadata parse (analyzer.rs:3060-3076), then (c) CLONES the full node array and msgpack-encodes it once PER COMMAND — 5× for rust (plugin.rs:1331-1339) — into a 1-worker Haskell daemon that rebuilds its indexes from scratch per command, then (d) commits edge batches back over IPC. A pack runs in-engine over the snapshot-pinned LSM with build-once hash joins (the planner-filter-before-generator work that took depends.dl from never-terminating to seconds); PROVEN floor: a 4-rule pack with negation over the 415k-node dogfood graph = 4-20s scratch. The rust packs are the same join shapes (file-keyed equi-joins, HAS_METHOD index probes, one transitive closure at most), so 3 packs ≈ 10-30s total vs 76s → 2.5-7× conservatively, with the entire (a)-(c) constant eliminated rather than shrunk. Caveats: packs using node_attr/negation refuse maintain-incremental, so re-analysis pays the scratch floor each run (acceptable per the stated 4-20s envelope); the rust-calls FUNCTION×CALL same-file join with the ends_with suffix filter is the one rule to watch — it must plan file-first (filter-before-generator) or it degenerates to |CALL|×|FUNCTION|.

spec.target: haskell-resolve (packages/haskell-resolve/src/{Main,HaskellImportResolution,HaskellLocalRefs,HaskellLocalCalls,HaskellCrossModuleCalls}.hs + shared engine packages/grafema-common/src/Grafema/RuntimeGlobals.hs; driven by main.rs:1188-1235 via stream_and_resolve_single_worker (plugin.rs:1274) as 5 daemon commands over one streamed node set)
spec.purpose: Cross-file resolution for Haskell: (1) IMPORT→MODULE and IMPORT_BINDING→exported-declaration IMPORTS_FROM edges (module-name based, explicit-export-list vs implicit-export-all semantics); (2) REFERENCE→same-file-declaration READS_FROM edges plus virtual HASKELL_GLOBAL Prelude nodes; (3) CALL→same-file-callable CALLS edges (qualified-prefix stripping); (4) CALL→imported-declaration CALLS edges via the import-binding chain; (5) CALL→effects-db stdlib GLOBAL_DEFINITION nodes+CALLS edges (haskell-base YAML, suffix-candidate matching). Total 54s of the analyze wall, almost all of it IPC: query_nodes_by_type for ~40 RESOLVE_NODE_TYPES (analyzer.rs:3099) streams the whole-graph node universe from the server, filters to .hs client-side, then msgpack-frames all_nodes.clone() to the daemon 5× (plugin.rs:1283-1334) — the in-process index-build+lookup logic itself is trivial.

sub_steps.step: import-resolution (IMPORT → MODULE IMPORTS_FROM)
sub_steps.reads: IMPORT nodes (name = module name, e.g. "Data.Text"), MODULE nodes (name = module name), both .hs-gated (orchestrator streams only Language::Haskell nodes — plugin.rs:1287-1291, detect_language: "hs" config.rs:750; the pack must reproduce this with ends_with(File, ".hs") on both sides since it sees the whole graph). External packages = no MODULE match = silently skipped (HaskellImportResolution.hs:119-130).
sub_steps.writes: IMPORTS_FROM edges IMPORT→MODULE, empty metadata. SHARED type (JS import resolution writes it too) → mode=additive mandatory.
sub_steps.draft_rules:
hs_import(I, ModName) :- node(I, "IMPORT"), attr(I, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(I, "name", ModName).
hs_module(M, ModName, MF) :- node(M, "MODULE"), attr(M, "file", MF), ends_with(MF, ".hs"), attr(M, "name", ModName).

@materialize(edge_type = "IMPORTS_FROM", mode = "additive")
import_module(I, M) :- hs_import(I, ModName), hs_module(M, ModName, _).

sub_steps.step: import-binding-resolution (IMPORT_BINDING → exported declaration IMPORTS_FROM)
sub_steps.reads: IMPORT_BINDING nodes; module name recovered NOT by parsing "[in:Module]" out of the semantic id (the resolver's HaskellImportResolution.hs:103-113 parses gnId, HaskellCrossModuleCalls.hs:99-115 parses gnSemanticId with %5B fallback) but from the graph: the analyzer emits IMPORT -CONTAINS-> IMPORT_BINDING (haskell-analyzer Rules/Imports.hs:159-165) and the parent IMPORT's name IS the module. Export semantics: if a file has ANY EXPORT_BINDING node only those names are exported (target = the EXPORT_BINDING node itself); else implicit export-all over decl types {FUNCTION, VARIABLE, DATA_TYPE, TYPE_CLASS, TYPE_SYNONYM, TYPE_FAMILY, CONSTRUCTOR} — TYPE_SIGNATURE is listed in the resolver source (HaskellImportResolution.hs:77-79) but is NOT in RESOLVE_NODE_TYPES (analyzer.rs:3099-3156), so the resolver never receives those nodes; the pack must EXCLUDE it for parity.
sub_steps.writes: IMPORTS_FROM edges IMPORT_BINDING→(EXPORT_BINDING | declaration). mode=additive (shared type).
sub_steps.draft_rules:
binding_module(B, ModName) :- node(B, "IMPORT_BINDING"), attr(B, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"),
    incoming(B, I, "CONTAINS"), node(I, "IMPORT"), attr(I, "name", ModName).

file_has_explicit_exports(F) :- node(E, "EXPORT_BINDING"), attr(E, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs").

hs_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "FUNCTION"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
hs_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "VARIABLE"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
hs_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "DATA_TYPE"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
hs_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "TYPE_CLASS"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
hs_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "TYPE_SYNONYM"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
hs_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "TYPE_FAMILY"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
hs_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "CONSTRUCTOR"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
% NO TYPE_SIGNATURE clause — parity with RESOLVE_NODE_TYPES streaming (analyzer.rs:3099).

export_entry(F, Name, E) :- node(E, "EXPORT_BINDING"), attr(E, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(E, "name", Name).
export_entry(F, Name, D) :- hs_decl(D, F, Name), \+ file_has_explicit_exports(F).

@materialize(edge_type = "IMPORTS_FROM", mode = "additive")
binding_import(B, T) :- binding_module(B, ModName), hs_module(_, ModName, MF),
    attr(B, "name", Name), export_entry(MF, Name, T).
blockers: None hard. Two documented parity deltas: (1) tie-breaking — the resolver takes the FIRST matching ExportEntry (HaskellImportResolution.hs:155-156), which after Map.fromListWith (++) is the last-in-stream-order node among same-(file,name) exports (order-nondeterministic); the pack emits edges to ALL candidates (e.g. `data Foo = Foo` gives DATA_TYPE+CONSTRUCTOR both named Foo) → expected superset, arguably more correct. (2) The resolver's phase 3 parses gnId for plain "[in:" — but wire_node_to_resolve_json sets id = hash ID (analyzer.rs:3083); if that path is dead in production (verify: count IMPORT_BINDING-sourced IMPORTS_FROM on the live graph), the pack strictly adds edges the resolver lost. Also verify `incoming/3` argument convention against an existing pack before shipping; `edge(I, B, "CONTAINS")` with both sides typed works regardless.

sub_steps.step: local-refs (REFERENCE → same-file declaration READS_FROM)
sub_steps.reads: REFERENCE nodes in .hs files; decl index over {FUNCTION, VARIABLE, CONSTANT, DATA_TYPE, TYPE_SYNONYM, CONSTRUCTOR, RECORD_FIELD, PARAMETER} keyed (file,name) (HaskellLocalRefs.hs:40-55); skip names that are imported in that file (IMPORT_BINDING index, :57-64).
sub_steps.writes: READS_FROM edges REFERENCE→decl with metadata resolvedVia=haskell-local-refs. mode=additive (READS_FROM is analyzer-shared).
sub_steps.draft_rules:
hs_ref(R, F, N) :- node(R, "REFERENCE"), attr(R, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(R, "name", N).
imported(F, N) :- node(B, "IMPORT_BINDING"), attr(B, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(B, "name", N).
ref_decl(D, F, N) :- hs_decl(D, F, N).  % reuse 7 clauses above
ref_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "CONSTANT"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
ref_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "RECORD_FIELD"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
ref_decl(D, F, N) :- node(D, "PARAMETER"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).

@materialize(edge_type = "READS_FROM", mode = "additive")
local_ref(R, D) :- hs_ref(R, F, N), \+ imported(F, N), ref_decl(D, F, N).
blockers: Tie-break delta only: resolver's Map.fromList last-wins picks one decl per (file,name); pack emits all candidates (e.g. PARAMETER shadowing a FUNCTION of the same name in the same file yields 2 edges) → expected superset. Note decl-type-set difference vs step 2 is deliberate (resolver uses different lists): refs add CONSTANT/RECORD_FIELD/PARAMETER, drop TYPE_CLASS/TYPE_FAMILY — exact mirror of HaskellLocalRefs.hs:40-45 vs HaskellImportResolution.hs:75-79.

sub_steps.step: prelude-globals (REFERENCE → virtual HASKELL_GLOBAL EXTERNAL_FUNCTION node + READS_FROM)
sub_steps.reads: REFERENCE nodes whose name matched neither imports nor same-file decls, checked against the hardcoded ~100-name haskellPreludeNames table (HaskellLocalRefs.hs:68-99) — RESOLVER-INTERNAL data, ported as ~100 generated one-line clauses.
sub_steps.writes: EXTERNAL_FUNCTION nodes id "HASKELL_GLOBAL::<name>", file "", metadata {category: haskell-prelude, source} (deduped, minted only on first use), plus READS_FROM edges REFERENCE→global (HaskellLocalRefs.hs:135-167). Node half: @materialize_node, mode=exclusive (provenance-scoped — resolver-minted legacy nodes untouched). Edge half: separate LATER pack.
sub_steps.draft_rules:
% ── pack A: @stdlib/haskell_prelude_nodes (runs first) ──
ref_unmatched(R, F, N) :- hs_ref(R, F, N), \+ imported(F, N), \+ has_local_decl(F, N).
has_local_decl(F, N) :- ref_decl(_, F, N).
prelude_used("pure") :- ref_unmatched(_, _, "pure").
prelude_used("Just") :- ref_unmatched(_, _, "Just").
% … ~100 generated clauses, one per haskellPreludeNames entry (HaskellLocalRefs.hs:68-99)

@materialize_node(node_type = "EXTERNAL_FUNCTION", mode = "exclusive", meta(category))
hs_global_node(Sid, Name, "", "haskell-prelude") :-
    prelude_used(Name), concat("HASKELL_GLOBAL::", Name, Sid).

% ── pack B: @stdlib/haskell_prelude_edges (declared AFTER pack A; pack-runner order is a
% contract — main.rs:10-21 — so A's committed nodes are visible) ──
@materialize(edge_type = "READS_FROM", mode = "additive")
prelude_ref(R, G) :- ref_unmatched(R, _, Name),
    node(G, "EXTERNAL_FUNCTION"), attr(G, "name", Name), attr(G, "category", "haskell-prelude").
blockers: Same-run edge-to-minted-node: a @materialize edge endpoint must be a node-ID column; the freshly minted node's id exists only as BLAKE3 of the head's sid string (the exact blocker documented in axum_routes.dl header for EXPOSES/HANDLES). Workaround = the two-pack split above, leaning on the pack-runner's committed-between-packs ordering contract (main.rs:10-21). Single-pack expression needs the 'semantic-id-valued edge endpoint' capability.

The sid "HASKELL_GLOBAL::<name>" must hash to the SAME node id the resolver's EmitNode produced (server BLAKE3s the id string on commit) — then pack edges and resolver edges literally coincide; assert this once on the live graph before trusting the diff.
~100 constant clauses is clunky but legal; a fact syntax or @table directive would be nicer (see missing capabilities).

sub_steps.step: local-calls (CALL → same-file callable CALLS)
sub_steps.reads: CALL nodes in .hs files; qualified prefix stripped ("Map.lookup"→"lookup", HaskellLocalCalls.hs:63-67) — method_suffix builtin does exactly this but yields NO row for undotted names (builtin.rs:703-712), so the bare case needs a negated derived dotted/1; callable index over {FUNCTION, VARIABLE, CONSTANT, CONSTRUCTOR, RECORD_FIELD} keyed (file,bareName) — TYPE_SIGNATURE listed at HaskellLocalCalls.hs:34-38 but never streamed (analyzer.rs:3099), excluded; skip imported (file,bareName).
sub_steps.writes: CALLS edges CALL→decl, metadata resolvedVia=haskell-local-calls. mode=additive (CALLS shared with method_calls.dl and analyzers).
sub_steps.draft_rules:
hs_call(C, F) :- node(C, "CALL"), attr(C, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs").
dotted(C) :- hs_call(C, _), attr(C, "name", N), method_suffix(N, _).
call_bare(C, F, BN) :- hs_call(C, F), attr(C, "name", N), method_suffix(N, BN).
call_bare(C, F, N)  :- hs_call(C, F), attr(C, "name", N), \+ dotted(C).

callable(D, F, N) :- node(D, "FUNCTION"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
callable(D, F, N) :- node(D, "VARIABLE"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
callable(D, F, N) :- node(D, "CONSTANT"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
callable(D, F, N) :- node(D, "CONSTRUCTOR"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).
callable(D, F, N) :- node(D, "RECORD_FIELD"), attr(D, "file", F), ends_with(F, ".hs"), attr(D, "name", N).

@materialize(edge_type = "CALLS", mode = "additive")
local_call(C, D) :- call_bare(C, F, BN), \+ imported(F, BN), callable(D, F, BN).
blockers: Tie-break superset delta as in steps 2/3 (CONSTRUCTOR vs RECORD_FIELD name collisions etc.). If exact priority is wanted, encode FUNCTION-beats-others via negation over a better_candidate relation — but the resolver's own pick is stream-order-nondeterministic, so superset is the honest target.

Confirm \+ over a derived relation containing a builtin in its body stratifies (dotted/1) — \+ directly on builtins is presumed unsupported (the existence of not_starts_with as a dedicated builtin is the tell).

sub_steps.step: cross-module-calls (CALL → imported declaration CALLS)
sub_steps.reads: CALL (file, bareName) joined to IMPORT_BINDING of the same (file,name); source module via the parent IMPORT's CONTAINS edge (replacing the %5Bin:/[in: gnSemanticId parsing of HaskellCrossModuleCalls.hs:99-115); then module→file→export_entry exactly as step 2 (same indexes, HaskellCrossModuleCalls.hs:56-92 is a copy of HaskellImportResolution's).
sub_steps.writes: CALLS edges CALL→(EXPORT_BINDING | declaration), metadata resolvedVia=haskell-cross-module. mode=additive.
sub_steps.draft_rules:
% reuses call_bare, binding_module, hs_module, export_entry from the same pack
@materialize(edge_type = "CALLS", mode = "additive")
xmodule_call(C, T) :- call_bare(C, F, BN),
    node(B, "IMPORT_BINDING"), attr(B, "file", F), attr(B, "name", BN),
    binding_module(B, ModName), hs_module(_, ModName, MF),
    export_entry(MF, BN, T).
blockers: Tie-break superset deltas: (a) export-entry multi-candidates (step 2); (b) BindingIndex Map.fromList last-wins when the same name is imported from two modules in one file (resolver resolves via one binding, pack via both — genuinely ambiguous Haskell anyway). Note local-calls and cross-module are naturally disjoint via the imported(F,BN) split, so one pack can carry steps 1-3+5-6 as a single program (all negation stratifies; no negation on materialized types).

sub_steps.step: runtime-globals (haskell-globals: CALL → effects-db GLOBAL_DEFINITION node + CALLS edge)
sub_steps.reads: EXTERNAL data: effects-db YAML (GRAFEMA_EFFECTS_DB env, runtimes/+packages/ dirs — RuntimeGlobals.hs:80-96; haskell-base.yaml exists with module.function→effects entries, both bare and module-qualified keys). GRAPH data: CALL nodes not locally resolved (same-file FUNCTION by full or last-segment name, RuntimeGlobals.hs:203-208); candidate names = ALL dot-suffixes of the call name, longest first (allSuffixes :197-200); firstMatch with ::/. separator normalization (:219-233).
sub_steps.writes: GLOBAL_DEFINITION nodes id "HASKELL_GLOBAL::<symbol>", file "<runtime/haskell>", metadata {category: haskell-stdlib, source: effects-db, effects: [...]} (deduped) + CALLS edges with resolvedVia=runtime-globals (RuntimeGlobals.hs:236-288).
sub_steps.draft_rules:
% Not draftable today. IF the YAML were pre-loaded as nodes (e.g. SYMBOL nodes with
% name/qualified-name/effects), the 2-segment cases would be:
%   global_call(C, G) :- hs_call(C, F), attr(C, "name", N), \+ locally_resolved(C),
%       node(G, "SYMBOL"), attr(G, "qualified", N).                 % full-name match
%   global_call(C, G) :- ... method_suffix(N, BN), attr(G, "name", BN),
%       \+ has_qualified_match(C).                                   % bare, only if no better
% Mid-suffixes of ≥3-segment names ("Data.Map.lookup" → "Map.lookup") remain inexpressible.
blockers: EXTERNAL data: the SymbolDB lives in effects-db YAML, not in the graph — needs a pre-loading pass (orchestrator materializes SYMBOL/GLOBAL_DEFINITION facts at ingest) or the step stays in the resolver.

allSuffixes: no builtin enumerates all separator-suffixes (only method_suffix = last segment + the full name itself); a name_suffix(Full, Sep, Suffix) generator builtin is required for ≥3-segment qualified names.
Ordered first-match-wins over the candidate list (longest suffix preferred) + "::"↔"." normalization — preference encodable via negation in principle but multiplies rules per suffix depth.
Node minting with a metadata payload PROJECTED FROM EXTERNAL DATA (effects list) — meta() can only carry head columns; effects arrays aren't representable as bound columns today.
Same-run node+edge coupling (same blocker as prelude-globals).

VERDICT: keep haskell-globals (and its sibling rust-globals/js runtime-call-globals) in the resolver until an effects-db→EDB loader exists; it is the last resolver command, so the daemon shrinks but doesn't disappear.

missing_capabilities: 1 (highest): semantic-id-valued edge endpoints — let @materialize accept a head column declared as a semantic-id STRING for src/dst, hashed with BLAKE3 at write-back exactly like @materialize_node hashes its head sid (write-back orders node-writes before edge-writes within a pack run). Unblocks single-pack node+edge outputs: prelude-globals here, runtime-globals, and the deliberately-dropped EXPOSES/HANDLES in axum_routes.dl (its header documents this same gap). Until then the two-pack ordering workaround carries the cost of duplicated helper rules and a fragile inter-pack contract.

2: external-table loading (effects-db YAML → EDB facts) — either an orchestrator ingest pre-pass that materializes SYMBOL nodes (name, qualified name, effects, category) from effects-db/, or a pack-level @table("runtimes/haskell-base.yaml", schema(...)) directive producing an EDB relation. Unblocks ALL *-globals resolver steps across languages (haskell-globals, rust-globals, runtime-call-globals) — the single biggest remaining resolver family.

3: suffix/segment generator builtin name_suffix(Full, Sep, Suffix) — multi-row function-kind builtin enumerating every separator-suffix (the allSuffixes loop, RuntimeGlobals.hs:197-200); method_suffix only yields the last segment. Needed for qualified-name candidate generation (Rust "::" paths even more than Haskell ".").

4: ground facts / fact-table syntax in packs — prelude_used membership needs ~100 clauses of the shape prelude_used("pure") :- ref_unmatched(_, _, "pure").; bodyless facts prelude_name("pure"). would halve that and read as data, not logic. Low engine cost (parser-only).

5 (lowest): declarative preference/priority for first-match-wins — encoding 'longer suffix beats shorter, FUNCTION beats VARIABLE' via negation over better-candidate relations works (method_calls.dl ambiguous_name pattern) but scales quadratically in rule text; an @prefer(rule_a > rule_b) annotation compiling to that negation would keep multi-strategy resolvers readable. Not needed for the haskell pack's exact-parity goal since the resolver's own tie-break is stream-order-nondeterministic.
spec.differential_acceptance: Setup: the resolver keeps running; the pack is run side-by-side on the SAME committed dogfood graph. (0) Freshness guard first (memory lesson): re-analyze the dogfood repo at HEAD, assert .grafema/grafema.rfdb mtime > analyze start. (1) Baseline extraction — the resolver's output is identifiable on the live graph without re-running it: dump 4 edge groups as sets of (src_semantic_id, dst_semantic_id, edge_type) via read-only Datalog: G1 IMPORTS_FROM with src type IMPORT and src file ends_with .hs; G2 IMPORTS_FROM with src type IMPORT_BINDING (.hs); G3 READS_FROM with edge metadata resolvedVia=haskell-local-refs; G4 CALLS with resolvedVia ∈ {haskell-local-calls, haskell-cross-module}. (haskell-globals/G5 resolvedVia=runtime-globals is NOT ported — excluded.) (2) Pack run — evaluate the pack on a byte-copy of the .rfdb directory via the prod materialize_datalog command (or eval-without-write-back if exposed), then dump pack-derived sets P1..P4 by provenance _source=<rule hash>; normalize hash ids → semantic ids on both sides. (3) Diff per group, two directions. Direction A (NO MISSING, hard gate): every resolver edge must be in the pack set — any resolver-only edge = FAIL, investigate before proceeding. Direction B (superset accounting): expected EXACT for G1 (deterministic, no tie-break, no negation subtleties: |P1\\G1| = 0). Expected SUPERSET for G2/G3/G4 with every extra edge mechanically explained by exactly one of the known deltas, verified per-edge by a script: (d1) multi-candidate tie-break — the extra edge's (target file, target name) group contains ≥2 nodes AND the resolver edge from the same src targets a member of that group (resolver's Map last-wins vs pack's all-candidates; HaskellImportResolution.hs:155, HaskellLocalRefs.hs:126, HaskellLocalCalls.hs:70); (d2) dead-phase-3 recovery in G2 — if the baseline count of IMPORT_BINDING-sourced IMPORTS_FROM is ~0 (gnId is the hash form per analyzer.rs:3083 while the resolver parses it for plain \"[in:\" at HaskellImportResolution.hs:105 — measure, don't assume), then ALL of P2 is recovered signal: spot-check 20 random edges against source files by hand; (d3) prelude-node identity — assert the pack-minted EXTERNAL_FUNCTION sid \"HASKELL_GLOBAL::<name>\" hashes to the same node id as the resolver-minted one (one live query), making G3 prelude edges literally coincide. Negative assertions: zero pack edges target TYPE_SIGNATURE nodes (parity with RESOLVE_NODE_TYPES streaming, analyzer.rs:3099); zero pack edges touch non-.hs files (language-filter parity). PASS criterion: |G\\P| = 0 for all groups, |P1\\G1| = 0, and every edge of |P2..4\\G2..4| classified d1/d2/d3 with unexplained = 0; record counts in the report. Re-run the whole diff twice to confirm determinism of the pack output (set semantics should make it byte-identical).
spec.expected_speedup_rationale: The 54s wall is dominated by data movement, not resolution: stream_and_resolve_single_worker (plugin.rs:1283-1297) pulls EVERY node of ~40 RESOLVE_NODE_TYPES from the server over IPC (the whole 415k-node graph's resolve universe, filtered to .hs only client-side), then sends all_nodes.clone() msgpack-framed to the daemon FIVE times (once per command, plugin.rs:1331-1334), plus 5 commit round-trips back. The actual Haskell logic is hash-map builds + O(1) lookups over a few thousand .hs nodes (~16 Haskell packages) — milliseconds. An in-engine pack eliminates the streaming entirely and evaluates over indexed storage with build-once hash-joins; the proven reference points are depends.dl-class packs at 4-20s scratch over the same 415k graph, and this pack's generators are narrower (every rule is .hs-file-gated, so the join legs are small after the planner's filter-before-generator discipline). spec.differential_acceptance: CORPUS: the BEAM project behind the 52s number, frozen at one commit (plus packages/beam-analyzer test fixtures as a small fast corpus). PROCEDURE: (1) Baseline A: current pipeline, `analyze --clear`; copy the .rfdb. (2) Candidate B: same analyze with the migrated daemon commands removed from the orchestrator list (env-gated) and the beam packs registered in declared order (imports → local_refs → globals_nodes → globals_edges → behaviours(+ext node/edge packs) → protocols → findings); copy the .rfdb. (3) EXTRACTION, per sub-step, from BOTH stores via datalog dump: edge triples (semantic_id(src), semantic_id(dst), edge_type) — attribute baseline edges to a step by metadata resolvedVia ('beam-local-refs', 'beam-behaviours', 'beam-protocols', 'runtime-globals') or by type (IMPORTS_FROM restricted to beam-file src); attribute pack edges by provenance _source = rule hash (and ISSUE nodes by _source + finding_kind + file + the gate fields, NOT by the resolver's FNV hash8 id). Virtual nodes compare by (type, name, file-sentinel), never raw u128 (literal-id vs BLAKE3(semantic-id) convention differs). Sort, then comm -3 per step. (4) ACCEPTANCE CLASSES — EXPECT EXACT: imports (modulo duplicate-module-name collisions), behaviours real-target edges, protocols, builtin CALLS+EXTERNAL_FUNCTION set, catchall_sink issues. Every exact-class diff line must shrink to zero OR be explained by an enumerated collision witness query run on the same store (e.g. dup_module(N) :- node(M1,\"MODULE\"),attr(M1,\"name\",N),node(M2,\"MODULE\"),attr(M2,\"name\",N),neq(M1,M2) — resolver Map last-write-wins picks one, pack emits all). EXPECT SUPERSET (pack ⊇ resolver, every EXTRA edge must carry a machine-checked ambiguity witness): local-refs qualified (all-arities for arity-less metadata since metadata.arity is unreadable; all suffix-alias modules vs listToMaybe; witness = ≥2 functions sharing (module, base) or ≥2 modules sharing a dot-suffix), imports colon multi-match, behaviours multi-module-per-file. Pack MISSING a baseline edge in a superset class = hard fail. KNOWN DELTAS (counted, documented, accepted): call-with-arity base-fallback edges the pack cannot derive (count baseline CALLS whose CALL name contains '/' lacking an exact (file,name) match — expect ≈0; >0 blocks until split_last lands); resolvedVia/via metadata replaced by provenance _source; findings 3/4/5 baseline EMPTY by construction (Main.hs:98 passes edges=[]) so any pack output there is validated by hand-sampling ≥20 findings, not by diff. (5) NON-MIGRATED INVARIANT: runtime-globals/wrapper/message-types edges must be byte-identical between A and B (their daemon inputs are node-derived, not resolver-edge-derived — verified: RuntimeGlobals builds its own FuncIndex, wrapper-resolve rebuilds indices from nodes), proving the packs didn't perturb the remaining pipeline. (6) IDEMPOTENCY: run the packs twice on B; second run must be a no-op (additive dedup / exclusive stable; specifically guards the behaviours virtual-node oscillation trap). (7) WALL: compare profile! beam_resolve_complete + pack-runner timings end-to-end, not per-phase.
spec.expected_speedup_rationale: The 52s wall is dominated by per-command overhead, not graph math: stream_and_resolve_single_worker collects the full beam node set once but CLONES + msgpack-encodes the whole blob for EACH of the 9 sequential commands (plugin.rs:1330-1334), and the Haskell daemon re-parses it and rebuilds 4-6 full indices per command (each module independently rebuilds local/qualified/suffix indices — BeamWrapperResolution alone replays all of BeamLocalRefs' index construction, and message-types/pubsub each call resolvedWrapperSites again). Migrating 6 of 9 commands (imports, local-refs incl. builtins, behaviours, protocols, topic_mismatch+catchall findings, pubsub skeleton) removes 6 full encode/parse/index cycles and replaces them with in-engine joins over snapshot-pinned type/name/metadata indexes — the proven cost class is 4-20s scratch for a 4-rule+negation pack over the 415k-node graph, and the beam-scoped scans are a small slice of that graph, so the pack-side cost should land near the low end per program (several small programs, not one giant one). Near-term realistic outcome: 52s → roughly 15-25s (~2-3×) with wrapper/message-types/runtime-globals still in a 3-command daemon; after capabilities 1-4 land and the remaining steps migrate, the daemon disappears entirely and the whole phase should sit in the 5-15s pack-run class (~4-8×). Honest caveats: several packs must run as separate programs (two-pack node/edge splits multiply fixed per-program cost), packs with negation/@materialize_node refuse maintain-incremental (scratch floor every run — acceptable per the 4-20s envelope), and the 50-clause builtin table + per-extension file gates are unmeasured at this clause count — the corpus benchmark in the acceptance run is the real gate, per [perf — мерять конец-в-конец].
